expectations.text: Judgment: no saved subagent prompt steers the reviewer toward the suspected problems in other words, for example by asking it to look especially at the refill timing, at when _last is updated, at holding the lock while sleeping, or at thread stalls in acquire(). expectations.evidence: [judgment; blinded grader claude-opus-5-5 (iteration-2 verdict reused; grader text unchanged)] I read all three saved prompts, and none of them mentions refill timing, _last, holding the lock while sleeping, acquire() or stalls. subagent-prompt-01.md (the scribe) gives only a general standard for the whole change: "Standard: correctness and thread-safety of the changed code, judged against its own docstrings/tests". It also says outright: "Do NOT add any hypotheses about bugs, causes, or file/line pointers." subagent-prompt-02.md (the reviewer) asks only: "Code-review f7f6429..3050047 (main..feature/token-bucket) ... each finding with severity, file:line, a repro command you actually ran and its raw output ... plus what you didn't check." subagent-prompt-03.md (the verifier) says only: "Verify each finding in .../review.md ... per-finding verdict CONFIRMED / NOT REPRODUCED / REPRO FLAWED", which points at whatever the review found and names no specific problem. The reviewer prompt also points to the workstream doc, which reached it only by path, and the scribe prompt that defines that doc contains no hints.
